headline: UN staffer death in Ansar Allah custody -- Mohammad el Shami (OHCHR Yemen), held since June 6 2024

fault_line: Spy-network accusation vs arbitrary detention: are detained aid workers a security case or hostages of the Yemen war?

sections.what_happened: [MISSED CATCH-UP -- SATURDAY, NOT IN-WINDOW] Mohammad el Shami, a Yemeni staff member of the UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR) in Yemen, died in Ansar Allah detention after being arbitrarily held since June 6, 2024, when he and 60+ UN/NGO workers were detained and accused of belonging to an 'American-Israeli spy network'. His family was informed only recently, more than a month after his death, with no explanation of cause or circumstances. Turk demanded 'full transparency' and an 'urgent, independent and thorough investigation', plus immediate unconditional release of all other detained UN personnel (including seven OHCHR colleagues). Guterres said he was 'appalled' and echoed the investigation call. El Shami is the SECOND UN staff member to die in Ansar Allah detention, after a World Food Programme worker in February 2025. 72 UN staffers and NGO workers detained in total (AJ); 71 UN personnel remained in detention as of mid-October (UN via Saudi Gazette); Yemen's prime minister holds the Ansar Allah fully responsible. No Ansar Allah comment on the death itself located. CAUSE OF DEATH IS UNVERIFIED -- no cause has been stated by any side.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (T1); Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA); UN OHCHR/UN bodies (T1, primary statements); Sky News (T2) and Euronews (T3) relays of the same UN statements
sections.what_disputed: Ansar Allah position (standing, not a comment on this death): detainees belong to a US-Israeli spy network; humanitarian work used as intelligence cover -- both claims made without evidence, per Reuters. SOCIAL CLAIM CONFLICT: a Blinx reel surfaced in the demand check calls el Shami the 'third' UN victim; the UN Secretary-General's statement says SECOND (after WFP Feb 2025) -- the UN count is used here, the Blinx count is not.
sections.why_matters: The UN's second dead staffer in Ansar Allah custody: held since June 2024, family told a month after his death, no cause given -- and 70+ UN staff still detained.
sections.context: Background: UN staffer death in Ansar Allah custody -- Mohammad el Shami (OHCHR Yemen), held since June 6 2024; UN demands investigation (Saturday statements; missed by all Nov 1 scans until this one)
